evidence: Independent implementation of the documented single-outcome logistic CRM and uniform-slope posterior. Native archive inspected as data without executing the Windows installer or model. The archive contains a compiled native engine and Java GUI; no model source was recovered. Native random-seed or estimator parity is not claimed.

sources.role: Application identity, version, download and guides.

Original installer archive. Configuration confirms fixed intercept, asymptotes, cohort and stopping controls. Native output strings include slope moments and Psi, confirming a two-outcome association component. Original binaries and guides are not redistributed.

Pages 13-20: single/both-outcome modes, target selection, logistic curve family, slope prior, fixed asymptotes, shared dose transformation when both outcomes are active, escalation cap and stopping criteria. Page21 section3.2.4 specifies corrected extreme-dose extra-allocation probabilities and clipping.
Goodman example skeleton, trial settings and native simulation comparisons; documents differences between software versions and the Braun example.
Single-outcome continual reassessment method cited by the official guide.
Bivariate extension cited by the official guide. The joint kernel and native association prior remain to be verified.

limitations: The guide states that two-outcome mode averages the separately transformed toxicity and efficacy dose vectors. Two independent single-outcome fits therefore do not establish a faithful bivariate implementation. The guide also does not resolve whether native dose decisions use posterior mean probability or probability at the posterior mean slope; Python returns both explicitly.
validation_reference: tools/reference_bcrm.R independently integrates the documented scalar posterior in base R for the Goodman skeleton, bounded asymptotes, and concentrated and boundary posterior cases. Counts are synthetic audit data, not native simulation results.
